issues.issue: Unnumbered Essex figure is not printed Chapter XCVII; it precedes planetary-hour tables.
Printed 13 May 1644 time and historical calendar have not been independently recast.
Named Robert Earl of Essex does not imply an authenticated contemporaneous forecast.
Physical appearance and temperament by sign are retrospective source assertions.
Planetary house, dignity, aspect and intercepted-sign calculations remain unchecked.
Moon trine Saturn separating versus applying square Mars is a sequence.
Mars is assigned multiple topics, not multiple independently observed results.
Loss, honor, betrayal, danger and opposition require different success metrics.
London opponents and alleged pretended friendships have no identified witnesses.
Additional predictions referenced but not specified cannot be scored.
Early prosperity is a counterweight to a wholly negative expedition narrative.
Claim that observers mocked a previous forecast has no separate dated record.
Personal receipt of bad news on September 8 is author-reported only.
Historic England confirms Essex escaped by sea Sept 1, while his army surrendered weaponry Sept 2.
Historic England draws on contemporary Essex letter, Edward Walker and Richard Symonds.
Other capitulation articles and alleged misconduct are not independently adjudicated.
External military-event corroboration is not verification of advance astrology.
One named episode cannot be counted as many independent predictive cases.
Numeric planetary-hour tables and subsequent printed XCVII remain unprocessed.
No independent complete transcription, ephemeris recast or predictive validation.
